ivr.status: provider-neutral design; confirm Google Voice or replacement platform feature support before implementation
ivr.opening: Thank you for calling CAD Guardian. You have drawings due. We keep them moving. Choose the option that best matches the business consequence you need to solve.

routes.name: Drawing deadline or package rescue
routes.prompt: Press 1 if a drawing, model or issue package is behind, failing review or due soon.
questions: Exact due date and time zone
routes.handoff: Immediate ring during business hours; after-hours capture plus priority SMS to owner
routes.sla: Acknowledge within 30 minutes during declared coverage; callback commitment only after source preflight
routes.sms: CAD Guardian received your drawing-deadline request. Reply with company, due date/time, platform and a secure file-link invitation. Do not text confidential files.

routes.name: Automation and systems
routes.prompt: Press 2 for AutoCAD, Revit, Inventor, Vault, batch processing, CAD/.NET automation or engineering-system integration.
routes.sms: CAD Guardian received your automation inquiry. Reply with the workflow, platform, volume and business consequence. We will recommend the correct paid first step.

routes.name: Existing client or active delivery
routes.prompt: Press 3 if you are an existing client or calling about an active CAD Guardian delivery.
routes.sms: Your active-delivery message is logged. Include the engagement or project ID and urgency. Do not send credentials or controlled files by text.

routes.name: Partnership, referral or vendor onboarding
routes.prompt: Press 4 for partnerships, referrals, subcontracting, vendor registration or procurement.
routes.sms: Thank you for the CAD Guardian partnership inquiry. Reply with organization, opportunity type and deadline.

routes.name: Recruiting and employment opportunities
routes.prompt: Press 5 for a role, contract, interview or recruiting inquiry involving Thomas Smith.
routes.handoff: Separate recruiting pipeline; never mix with consulting CRM conversion metrics
routes.sms: Thank you. Please email the full role, end client, employment model, compensation, requisition and representation terms. Duplicate submissions are not authorized.

routes.name: General
routes.sms: CAD Guardian received your message. Reply with your organization, reason for calling and preferred callback window.

afterHours.greeting: CAD Guardian is currently outside live coverage. If drawings are due within 48 hours, press 1 and state the exact deadline first. Otherwise leave your name, organization, business consequence, platform and callback window.

positioningPillars.name: Delivery certainty
positioningPillars.message: CAD Guardian controls the path from available evidence to a defensible drawing/model package.

positioningPillars.name: Repeatable engineering output
positioningPillars.message: We automate repeated CAD, BOM and document work without hiding exceptions or removing ownership.

positioningPillars.name: Safe modernization
positioningPillars.message: We preserve trusted behavior, add regression evidence and modernize one bounded CAD utility or integration at a time.

positioningPillars.name: Governed handoff
positioningPillars.message: Standards, dependencies, review states and acceptance become explicit enough for internal and external contributors to perform reliably.

qualificationScorecard.question: What happens if the problem remains?
qualificationScorecard.strong: Deadline, margin, release, client or production consequence is explicit.
qualificationScorecard.weak: General interest or technology exploration only.

qualificationScorecard.question: How often and at what volume does it occur?
qualificationScorecard.strong: Recurring package, product, job or handoff.
qualificationScorecard.weak: Unrelated one-offs with no common operating contract.

qualificationScorecard.question: Who owns the workflow and accepts change?
qualificationScorecard.weak: No one can approve scope, rules or exceptions.

qualificationScorecard.question: What representative files and accepted outputs exist?
qualificationScorecard.strong: Trusted examples and failure cases available.

qualificationScorecard.question: Can the necessary systems and files be inspected safely?
qualificationScorecard.weak: No access, no export and no owner.

qualificationScorecard.question: What is the cost of delay, touch time or rework?
Is CAD/engineering output central to the risk?
qualificationScorecard.strong: CAD/BIM/PDM, drawings, models, BOMs, documents or engineering workflow are primary.
qualificationScorecard.weak: Generic web/IT work with no CAD or engineering operating boundary.

objectionPosture.objection: We need a proposal before paying for discovery.
objectionPosture.response: A concise scope and commercial route are provided before purchase. The diagnostic is the paid work that establishes the evidence and implementation decision a reliable proposal requires.

objectionPosture.objection: Your rate is higher than drafting labor.
objectionPosture.response: The comparison is not hourly drafting. CAD Guardian sells controlled delivery, standards authority, QA evidence, automation and reduced key-person correction burden.
Only authorized references are public. We can show methods, anonymized evidence and bounded technical proofs without violating client trust.
AI may assist extraction or review. The paid outcome still requires source authority, exception handling, validation, professional boundaries and accountable release.

objectionPosture.objection: Start now and we will handle paperwork later.
objectionPosture.response: Urgency accelerates preflight; it does not remove written scope, payment, access and authority controls.

interviewQuestions: Which CAD and electrical design platforms are in production, and which versions?
What business workflows do the current scripts and applications protect?
Where do failures surface today: user desktop, batch queue, release process or downstream reporting?
What is the expected split among maintenance, modernization and net-new capability?
How are deployments tested and distributed to engineering users?
Which integrations and databases are systems of record?
What would a successful first 90 days change operationally?
opportunityExample.enterpriseNarrative: I work at the boundary where engineering users, CAD platforms and enterprise software must agree. My approach is to preserve trusted behavior, expose dependencies, add regression evidence and modernize one controlled workflow at a time. That reduces technical risk while producing visible operating improvements.
